biography: Born in Västervik, Sweden, Felix Rosenqvist's racing journey began, surprisingly, not on asphalt, but on ice. His father, a former ice racer, introduced him to the sport at a young age. Felix quickly displayed an uncanny ability to read the ice, mastering car control in the most treacherous conditions. However, a near-fatal accident during an ice race at age 16 pushed him towards circuit racing, a decision that undoubtedly saved his life, even though he still misses the thrill of the ice. His transition was seamless, proving his skill was universal. In 2023, he joined the F-USA series, seeking to solidify his legacy among the American racing giants. Although his early performances were less than stellar, his experience and never-say-die attitude has kept him going, even as younger drivers gain prominence.
drivingStyle: Rosenqvist's driving style is a blend of Scandinavian precision and raw aggression. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, often flirting with the edge of grip. He's a master of the 'Scandinavian flick,' adapting his ice racing experience to initiate controlled drifts on the asphalt. While this style is undeniably exciting, it also leads to occasional errors and inconsistencies, making him a high-risk, high-reward driver.

rivalries.reason: A clash of generations and driving styles. Rossi, a young prodigy, openly criticizes Rosenqvist's 'reckless' approach, while Rosenqvist dismisses her as 'too calculated' and lacking the guts to take risks.

A long-standing rivalry stemming from their Formula 3 days. Both drivers were fiercely competitive, often colliding on track. Alvarez, now a seasoned veteran like Rosenqvist, sees him as a personal benchmark and a constant reminder of their shared past.
Tanaka and Rosenqvist have butted heads over similar sponsorship deals. Tanaka's team has more money and has been able to outbid Rosenqvist on more than one occasion, leading to some frustration.

quirks: Always wears a specific pair of lucky blue socks under his racing suit, inherited from his ice racing father.
Listens to ABBA at full volume in his headphones exactly 30 minutes before every race, claiming it 'gets the Swedish aggression flowing'.
Insists on personally polishing his helmet visor before each session, believing it enhances his vision.
famousQuote: "You can't win a race by being polite. Sometimes, you have to throw caution to the wind and just go for it."
careerHighlight: Winning the Macau Grand Prix in 2014 after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying incident. He carved his way through the field with a series of daring overtakes, showcasing his exceptional car control and strategic brilliance.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2018. The mechanical failure caused his vehicle to skid into the wall, costing him and his team a certain victory.
